summary: Split-session upload workers triggering sustained 429s despite apparent quota availability
description:
Issue summary: Customer running large multi-region ingestion pipeline (split into short-lived worker sessions) started seeing persistent 429s for the /v1/embeddings endpoint after migrating parts of the workload to a Dedicated pool. Impact: Ingestion throughput dropped ~70%, backlog of files accumulated, downstream vector updates delayed. Environment: Dedicated pool -> dedicated-us-east-2, Hosted control plane, token-based auth, multiplexed short-lived API keys created by the customer's orchestration layer.

Observed behavior: Despite account quota appearing available in the Console and token-bucket metrics, the client receives high rate of 429 responses with Retry-After headers between 5-12s. Throttling persists even when total tenant token usage is below committed capacity. Customer suspects per-session accounting or a stale window aligning with their split-session worker pattern.

Expected behavior: Short-lived worker sessions that sequentially call the embeddings endpoint should be able to consume available tenant quota under standard burst smoothing settings without sustained 429s unless overall tenant capacity is exceeded.
steps_to_reproduce: Customer runs 200 parallel short-lived worker processes that each obtain an ephemeral API key from their orchestration service.
Each worker opens a connection and immediately POSTs a 128-item embeddings batch to /v1/embeddings and closes after completion.
Workers are sharded across two regions (us-east-2 and eu-west-1) that both route to the same Dedicated pool via smart-routing.
After ~3-5 minutes the clients start receiving 429s with Retry-After 5-12s despite per-tenant token counters showing available capacity.
Scaling down parallelism by 50% reduces 429 frequency, but not eliminating them entirely.
logs: 2026-03-10T15:12:03Z ERR throttle=tenant_quota_exceeded tenant_id=lyra-123 api_key=ephemeral-zz123 route=/v1/embeddings status=429 retry_after=8
observed: spike pattern aligned to ephemeral key TTL refresh; health-check probes from pool surfaced in tenant accounting during the same window
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: per-key token-bucket misattribution causing small ephemeral keys to hit low per-key windows while tenant window remains healthy.
Checked Console usage graphs: tenant-level tokens not exhausted; per-route metrics show high per-key rejection counts but no clear single noisy neighbor.

Correlation found between ephemeral key churn (high fanout of keys created and destroyed) and 429 onset. Suspect bucket reset/aggregation logic in edge proxies incorrectly mapping short-lived keys to the same internal bucket slice leading to hot-slot contention.

SRE ran replay of customer request pattern in staging with 300 short-lived keys; reproduced ~15% 429 rate with default burst windowing. When using long-lived key (single key), no 429s reproduced at same aggregate rate.
Added debug flags to quota-service to log internal bucket assignment for ephemeral keys; logs show multiple ephemeral keys being hashed to same shard during TTL boundary.
Related config: customer uses aggressive key TTL of 10s and orchestration spawns keys per worker start for easier isolation.
comments: 2026-03-10 16:05 - Aisha Patel (Support): Collected initial logs and tenant usage graphs from the customer. Asked for exact key TTL and orchestration pattern.

2026-03-10 18:30 - Connor Briggs (SRE): Replayed pattern in staging cluster and reproduced 429s. Noted per-key windows are small; suspect shard-hotting in quota-service. Captured shard mapping for ephemeral keys.

2026-03-11 09:12 - LyraSearch (Customer): Our workers create keys with TTL=10s and spawn ~200 processes every minute. We did this to ensure per-file isolation and easier retry semantics. Can we change anything on our side while you investigate?

2026-03-11 10:05 - Aisha Patel (Support): Suggested two immediate mitigations: 1) Increase key TTL to 5 minutes (reduce churn), 2) Use a small pool of rotating longer-lived keys per region. Customer will test increasing TTL and report.
2026-03-11 15:45 - LyraSearch (Customer): Increased TTL to 5m in staging; large decrease in 429s observed during a 20-minute run. Preparing change for prod tomorrow morning.

2026-03-12 11:20 - Connor Briggs (SRE): Engineering found that quota-service shard assignment uses hash(key_id) % N_shards and short-lived keys created in tight clusters can collide on shard boundaries. Proposed short-term fix: ignore keys with TTL < 30s for per-key strict windows and account them against a small pooled fallback bucket. Raised INT-42088 for implementation.
resolution: Workaround applied by customer (increased ephemeral key TTL to 5m). Engineering tracking short-term fix INT-42088 and longer-term resilience improvement in quota-service to avoid shard-hotting for high-churn key patterns.
resolution_notes: Customer saw immediate improvement in staging and applied TTL change in prod; throughput returned to expected levels with residual <2% 429s. Engineering to deploy fallback pooled-accounting behavior in next patch (refer to linked PR) and follow up with ETA. Postmortem scheduled after fix rollout.
